title: Tales of Genetics: Geek Monster
summary: NH tells the story of a college classmate, a 5-foot gamer who never trained and lived on sugary drinks yet had shredded massive forearms and calves, extremely long arms, a short torso and short legs: ideal powerlifting leverages he never used. The moral: genetics mean nothing unless applied, and hard work beats unused talent.
claims: A college classmate who never trained, never drank water and lived on Four Lokos and Mountain Dew had shredded, massive forearms and calves with low body fat
That classmate had hands near knee level, a short torso and tiny femurs: perfect deadlift and squat leverages, built like a lab-made powerlifter
Long-armed people usually have thin forearms, which made his massive forearms a striking outlier
Very gifted lifters rarely think about programming because everything comes easy; if you get them on a real regimen they become monsters
Despite repeated attempts I could never get him to try a deadlift because he did not care about physical activity
Huge hands with long fingers would have made grip strength natural for him
Talent is worthless if unapplied; by simply working you outdo many people, and outworking gifted people makes you better than them
Do not worry about your starting genetics; work hard and reflect and you can turn bad genetics into something sublime
